title: micro-handoff-notes-routing-auth-2026-06-18
content:
Micro handoff notes — platform engineering routing/auth/quotas (quick standup style)
Date: 2026-06-18
Owner: Maya Sanchez (notes)
Attendees: Jonah, Priya, Samir, Rae, Maya (remote)
Location: #pltfm-controlplane standup / quick sync

1) Quick context / goal for this week
- Keep two-zone control plane failover test stable while we land quota enforcement changes on canary.
- Measure routing tail latency impact when quota enforcement moves from pre-check to in-router cache (experiment).
- Triage auth token rotation edgecases flagged by QA (stale sessions + dedicated pools).

2) Control plane (Maya / Jonah)
- Progress:
  - Completed lightweight health-check shim for sidecar that surfaces per-route token cache hit rate (merged, PR 4567).
  - Canary rollout of new config-store patch to 5% of control-plane pods; no errors so far.
  - Burn-in tests show control-plane median sync time at 180ms (target <200ms) across eu-west-1 cluster.
- Blockers / risks:
  - One flaky test in operator that intermittently fails applying rate-limit policies (PLAT-2345). Need deeper investigation into CRD reconciliation ordering.
  - Observability gap: we still don't have a per-commit rollback trace tied to UI toggles; debugging deploy failures is manual.
- Action items:
  - Jonah to file follow-up on CRD reconciliation root cause and assign to infra-operator (due 2026-06-21).
  - Add a lightweight deploy-tag in the control-plane traces (Maya + SRE) — spike by 6/22.

3) Routing (Priya / Samir)
- Progress:
  - Experiment: moved soft quota enforcement check into routing layer cache for short-lived bursts. Early numbers: token throughput unchanged, 95th perc latency +8ms under 10% load; acceptable for canary.
  - Validated fallback policy: when routing cache misses, system falls back to async quota lookup without dropping request (works in staging).
- Metrics to watch:
  - 95th perc response time for routing decisions (baseline 45ms, canary 53ms)
  - Cache hit ratio target: >85% for prefix requests; currently 78% on canary (improve with TTL tuning).
- Blockers:
  - TTL tuning for prefix entries may cause cache churn and transient auth checks. Need a short experiment matrix.
- Action items:
  - Priya to run TTL sweep experiment (params: 30s, 60s, 120s) on canary for 24 hours and report (due 2026-06-20).
  - Samir to add synthetic load job to simulate traffic bursts at 3x baseline during TTL tests (due 6/20).

4) Auth (Rae + Ops)
- Progress:
  - QA surfaced a class of stale-session failures when KMS rotates keys mid-session for dedicated pools — reproduced locally.
  - Implemented a short-term mitigation: session metadata now persist the encrypted key version id so we can retry with fallback key (branch open).
- Blockers:
  - HSM environment for full repro is gated behind infra-provision (ticket INFRA-998). This slows validation for enterprise/private deployments.
- Open questions:
  - Long-term: do we keep key version pinned per session (simpler) or implement seamless key-version lookup with automatic re-encryption? Tradeoffs: complexity vs. risk during rotation windows.
- Action items:
  - Rae to draft proposal outlining tradeoffs and estimated dev effort (target 2026-06-24).
  - Ops to follow up on INFRA-998 with infra SRE (Jonah to own escalation).

5) Quotas (cross-cutting)
- Progress:
  - Canary enforcement enabled for 5% of customers; so far 3 blocked requests surfaced (business-impact low).
  - Created a lightweight quota forensic log that captures pre-enforce state + routed decision id for post-mortem.
- Observations:
  - Most blocked requests are due to sudden prefix-heavy traffic from a single partner (spikes). Need partner-level burst policies.
- Action items:
  - Create emergency partner-burst policy template and roll to canary (Priya + CS contact: @maria). Draft done by 6/21.
  - Add quota forensic logs to daily debug bundle consumed by SRE (Samir to add to pipeline).

6) Ops / Runbook / Incident readiness
- Short term notes:
  - Update runbook entry for quota enforcement fallback: include steps to temporarily disable enforcement for a customer and fallback to queued async lookup.
  - Add quick checklist for on-call: how to detect quota-induced routing latency (Dashboards + logs).
- Action items:
  - Samir to edit runbook and push as PR to ops-runbooks repo (due 6/22).
  - Maya to pair with on-call tomorrow for a 20m triage drill focused on control-plane slow sync (6/19).

7) Misc / Notes to self
- Keep a short list of tickets to watch: PLAT-2345 (CRD order), INFRA-998 (HSM repro), QUOTA-1120 (partner burst), AUTH-409 (session key fallback).
- Quick reminder: prototype for per-route cost breakdown (Optimize) will land next sprint; coordinate with product-hosted-api on SLO expectations.
- Slack threads to link in Confluence: #pltfm-controlplane -> thread 'deploy vs canary trace' and #pltfm-routing -> 'ttl-churn-observations'.

8) Open questions / parking lot
- Should routing layer keep a tiny persistent in-memory token bucket per customer to absorb bursts? (cost vs benefit)
- Is pinning key-version per session acceptable for enterprise customers who require zero-failure rotations?
- Do we need a quota preview API for customers to understand impact of pending enforcement changes? (product ask)

9) Next sync / cadence
- Quick follow-up next week (2026-06-25) — 25m deep-dive on TTL experiment results and auth key-version proposal.

---
Rough TODO summary (owner — target):
- Jonah: file CRD reconcilation follow-up (PLAT-2345) — 2026-06-21
- Maya + SRE: trace deploy-tag spike — 2026-06-22
- Priya: TTL sweep experiment & report — 2026-06-20
- Samir: synthetic burst job + runbook updates + add quota logs to debug bundle — 2026-06-22
- Rae: auth key rotation tradeoff proposal — 2026-06-24
- Priya + CS: partner-burst policy template — 2026-06-21

Notes: informal doc — collect results here and then formalize in the platform RFC if we pick a direction.
